Take this free CAT Coordinate Geometry online test — 10 exam-pattern MCQs with instant scoring and a worked explanation for every answer. The Coordinate Geometry chapter is a high-yield part of the CAT Quantitative Aptitude section, and a favourite in XAT, SNAP, NMAT and CMAT too. This guide explains what CAT Coordinate Geometry tests, the formulas and shortcuts worth memorising, the mistakes that cost marks, and a free 10-question online test you can take right now.

Take the quiz below first, read the explanation for anything you miss, then use the chapter e-book at the end for full, exam-level practice.

What CAT asks on Coordinate Geometry

Distance, section and midpoint, slope, equations of lines and the area of a triangle from coordinates.

Key formulas & shortcuts

  • Distance = √((x₂−x₁)²+(y₂−y₁)²).
  • Slope m = (y₂−y₁)/(x₂−x₁); line y = mx + c.
  • Parallel lines have equal slopes; perpendicular lines have m₁m₂ = −1.
  • Triangle area = ½|x₁(y₂−y₃)+x₂(y₃−y₁)+x₃(y₁−y₂)|.

Common mistakes to avoid

  • Mixing up the section-formula ratio order.
  • Sign errors in the slope of perpendicular lines.
  • Dropping the absolute value in the area formula.
